claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is single phase.
The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy has minimal inherent short-range order.
Atomic-size and modulus mismatches drive temperature-dependent short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range ordering creates local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions modulate dislocation mobility.
At lower elevated temperatures, short-range-ordered distorted regions act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Dislocation pinning by these regions increases yield strength at lower elevated temperatures.
At higher temperatures, stronger anharmonic lattice vibrations override the short-range-order pinning effect and facilitate dislocation motion.
Increasing anharmonic lattice vibrations at high temperature reduce the elastic modulus.
Increasing anharmonic lattice vibrations at high temperature enhance thermal expansion.
Annealing at 600–800 °C followed by rapid quenching will promote short-range order relative to the as-cast alloy.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the annealed alloy will have higher yield strength at lower elevated temperatures.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the annealed alloy will exhibit more pronounced elastic softening at temperatures approaching 1000 °C.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the annealed alloy will exhibit a higher thermal-expansion coefficient at temperatures approaching 1000 °C.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C when dislocation motion and anharmonic lattice vibrations dominate.
Phase instabilities may occur at temperatures above the proposed approximately 1000 °C applicability limit.
TEM and XRD can be used to evaluate differences in short-range order between the as-cast and annealed samples.
